氾.meaning: A clumsy office worker knocks over her water glass. As the <part>water drops</part> race across the desk, she slams her inky rubber <part>stamp</part> down to stop them. Now blue water creeps over every form, off the desk and across the carpet. The puddle has <kanji>spread out</kanji> over the whole office.
氾.on: Even the jar of <sound>hon</sound>ey on the shelf is bobbing along in it.
氾.kun: She hops onto her chair in her <sound>hee</sound>ls and orders the stain to stop, but it's a <sound>ro</sound>tten listener.

濫.meaning: A lifeguard is meant to <part>oversee</part> the hotel pool but dozes off in her tall chair. Someone leaves the hose running, the <part>water drops</part> become a flood, and the pool spills over the lobby and out into the street. Far too much water: <kanji>excessive</kanji>.
濫.on: Next door, the planes on the airport <sound>run</sound>way float like ducks.
濫.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat paddles through the lobby on a lilo and sings 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!' for no reason at all: recklessly.

塑.meaning: A badger who can't sleep pushes up wet <part>soil</part> at night and pats it into shapes. By dawn there's a clay garden on the lawn: a rose, a tulip, and a <part>moonflower</part> with its petals open wide. The gardener gasps: every bloom is a perfect <kanji>model</kanji>.
塑.on: The badger sits back on a lumpy mud <sound>so</sound>fa to admire his work.
塑.kun: The gardener carries the clay flowers out to her <sound>deck</sound> and props a little clay badger among them like a puppet.

瑠.meaning: A thief grabs the <part>king</part>'s blue jewel, but the stone seems to <part>detain</part> him all by itself: it's so heavy he can't lift it off its velvet cushion. The guards find him at dawn, still hugging it, gazing into the deep blue of the <kanji>lapis lazuli</kanji>.
瑠.on: A <sound>roo</sound>k on the window ledge caws at him all night.

璃.meaning: The <part>king</part> orders an <part>animal trap</part> made entirely of glass, so he can watch the beetles inside. It's so clear and smooth that the beetles can't climb out, and the king can't see it either, so he walks into it nose first. Everything about it is <kanji>glassy</kanji>.
璃.on: In a sulk, he sends it to the bottom of a coral <sound>ree</sound>f, where the fish admire their faces in it.

奈.meaning: In an old temple city sits a bronze statue so <part>large</part> that pigeons nest in its ears. Pilgrims climb the steps to the <part>altar</part> at its feet with flowers and rice cakes, and tame deer wander in to nibble them. You've arrived in <kanji>Nara</kanji>.
奈.on: A pilgrim leaves a warm <sound>na</sound>an on the altar, and a deer eats that too.
奈.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l pops up in the temple pond with a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation in its mouth, and the pilgrims wonder what on earth it wants.

沙.meaning: A beach is so proud of its sand that it rinses every grain in <part>water drops</part> and keeps only a <part>few</part>: the tiniest, softest ones. The rest are sent off to a gravel pit. Step on what's left and it squeaks like flour: <kanji>fine sand</kanji>.
沙.on: A seagull digs a whole <sound>sa</sound>rdine out of it, still shiny.
沙.kun: Another gull shakes <sound>soo</sound>t off its wings and buries its <sound>na</sound>an in it for later.

汰.meaning: A <part>plump</part> raccoon sits by the stream and swirls every snack it finds through the <part>water drops</part>: grapes, crackers, a sock. Anything that falls apart wasn't food anyway. Supper always comes after a good <kanji>washing</kanji>.
汰.on: At home, it does the dishes in a big <sound>tu</sound>b.
汰.kun: It rinses a toy <sound>o</sound>ctopus and its swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles too, then pays for its friends' supper: a treat.

埼.meaning: A giant gardener digs a pond and tips the <part>soil</part> into the sea, but it piles up in a <part>strange</part> long finger of land pointing out over the waves. Ships steer round it and seals sunbathe on its tip: a brand-new <kanji>cape</kanji>.
埼.on: A seal finds a big brass <sound>key</sound> buried at the very tip.
埼.kun: The seals snack on <sound>sa</sound>rdines and a <sound>ki</sound>wi washed up from a shipwreck.

刹.meaning: An old gardener spends forty years trimming one <part>tree</part> with tiny <part>scissors</part>, and a <part>dagger</part> for the tricky bits. Branch by branch it becomes roofs, steps and bells, until monks move in and start chanting. The garden now has a living <kanji>temple</kanji>.
刹.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter dog sleeps by its leafy gate.

茨.meaning: A donkey munches its way across a meadow of <part>grass</part>, always eyeing the <part>next</part> juicy patch, until its nose meets a tangle of hooked thorns. It backs off, braying. Every field has one corner nobody eats: the <kanji>briar</kanji>.
茨.on: The farmer cuts it back, hiding behind a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
茨.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeals the donkey, and trots off to the farmer's <sound>ba</sound>rbecue to sulk over a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

梨.meaning: A farmer's only <part>tree</part> keeps dropping fat golden fruit onto passing cars. Instead of saying sorry, he sells the dented fruit as 'car-polished' and makes a huge <part>profit</part>. His fortune is all thanks to his <kanji>pear tree</kanji>.
梨.on: He spends it on a diving trip to a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.
梨.kun: Back home, he serves sliced pears on <sound>na</sound>an to his <sound>shee</sound>p.

栃.meaning: Every autumn, a <part>tree</part> on the edge of a <part>cliff</part> lets go of <part>ten thousand</part> shiny brown nuts at once. They bounce down the rock like a drum roll and pile up on the beach, where the crabs try to crack them and give up. Nobody can eat a <kanji>horse chestnut</kanji>.
栃.kun: A <sound>to</sound>ddler on the beach stacks them into a tower and crowns it with a lump of <sound>chee</sound>se.

媛.meaning: A <part>woman</part> at the arcade spends her last coin on the <part>claw machine</part>. The claw wobbles, grabs, and drops a sparkly tiara into her hands. She puts it on, sees herself in the glass, and grins: a real <kanji>beauty</kanji>.
媛.on: She drives home with the <sound>en</sound>gine roaring and the tiara still on.
媛.kun: Her high <sound>hee</sound>l snaps on the doorstep, and she laughs at the <sound>me</sound>ss.

曽.meaning: An old ox with curled <part>horns</part> stands in the last <part>rice field</part> under the hot <part>sun</part>, staring at a shopping mall going up. 'This was all paddies,' he tells the bulldozers. Everything here used to be green, <kanji>formerly</kanji>.
曽.on: Now his field is a car wash, frothing with pink <sound>soa</sound>p.
曽.kun: He stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, then sneezes at the bubbles: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

貞.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> at the bottom of a fish tank finds a dripping <part>faucet</part> left by a plumber, with the plumber's wallet beside it. It drags the wallet all the way to the glass and taps until he comes back. An honest, <kanji>upright</kanji> clam.
貞.on: The plumber fixes a thank-you note to the tank with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
貞.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!' he sings, and drops a tiny plastic <sound>shee</sound>p into the tank as a reward: correct.

隻.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> runs a ferry on the duck pond, using a salty <part>pretzel</part> for a hull and a leaf for a sail. Soon she has a whole fleet, each pretzel numbered on the side. The harbour master counts them: twelve <kanji>vessels</kanji>.
隻.on: Each one patrols its own <sound>sec</sound>tor of the pond.

弥.meaning: Archery practice gets soggy: a broken <part>sprinkler</part> is spraying the target, and every arrow the girl fires from her <part>bow</part> knocks it so it sprays harder. Splash, gush, geyser: each shot makes it worse. She gets <kanji>increasingly</kanji> wet.
弥.on: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat watches it all from a dry rock.
弥.kun: She gives up and dances in the spray, yelling '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo!'

恭.meaning: Every year, the whole village lifts the oldest gardener's chair <part>together</part> and carries her round the square, while a <part>trickle</part> of rose petals falls from the windows. She waves and blushes. It's how they show <kanji>respect</kanji>.
恭.on: Her grandson shouts that next year they'll carry her all the way to <sound>Kyo</sound>to, stretching the start of the name as long as the parade.
恭.kun: The crowd chants '<sound>Oo</sound>-<sound>ya</sound>, <sound>oo</sound>-<sound>ya</sound>!' in time with each step.

薫.meaning: A grandpa tosses a handful of <part>grass</part> and herbs onto the <part>hot coals</part> in his stove and drops a <part>heavy</part> iron lid on top. Sweet smoke curls out of every crack, and the whole street sniffs and smiles. His is the most <kanji>fragrant</kanji> house in town.
薫.on: A moth in its co<sound>coon</sound> on the windowsill wakes up to sniff.
薫.kun: Even his <sound>ca</sound>lm pet <sound>o</sound>ctopus lifts one arm out of its tank to sniff it.

椎.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> lives in an evergreen <part>tree</part> covered in tiny spiky burs. She cracks one open and finds a sweet brown nut the size of a fingertip, then hoards a hundred more in an old boot. Her favourite snack is the <kanji>chinquapin</kanji>.
椎.on: She plucks the nuts out of their spiky shells with a pair of <sound>twee</sound>zers.
椎.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes at the dust, and a nut shoots out and bonks a napping <sound>chee</sound>tah on the nose.

逓.meaning: <part>Two</part> lizards pass a letter rolled in a <part>towel</part>. The first, at the top of a <part>cliff</part>, slides it down a <part>ramp</part> to the second at the bottom, who runs it on to a frog, who hops it to a duck. Claw to claw to beak: a <kanji>relay</kanji>.
逓.on: The letter is sealed shut with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
逓.kun: The duck stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, takes its turn, and <sound>wa</sound>ddles it to the post box.

藍.meaning: A dyer has to <part>oversee</part> a vat of crushed <part>grass</part> leaves soaking for days. When she finally dips a white sheet in, it comes out green, then, as the air touches it, slowly turns the deep blue of a night sky: <kanji>indigo</kanji>.
藍.on: She sells the cloth to a fashion show, and it struts down the <sound>run</sound>way.
藍.kun: Every model on the catwalk wears <sound>eye</sound> shadow to match it.

唄.meaning: A <part>shellfish</part> on the harbour rocks opens its <part>mouth</part> at sunset and sings a slow, sad song about a pearl it lost long ago. Sailors stop rowing to listen, and some wipe their eyes. Every night, the same old <kanji>ballad</kanji>.
唄.on: On the pier, a fisherman rings his <sound>bi</sound>ke bell in time.
唄.kun: The sailors hum along, '<sound>Oo</sound>,' and tap out the beat on an upturned <sound>tu</sound>b.

孔.meaning: A <part>child</part> crunches toffee so hard that a <part>zigzag</part> crack runs down her back tooth. The dentist peers in with a torch, gasps, and says a tiny mouse could move into that <kanji>cavity</kanji>.
孔.on: Her reward for being brave: a sugar-free ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
孔.kun: 'Say <sound>ah</sound>,' says the dentist, and plucks out a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an.

怨.meaning: A <part>sleeping cat</part> is woken by the neighbour's lawnmower at seven on a Sunday. She says nothing, but deep in her <part>heart</part> she remembers. For years she leaves muddy paw prints on his car every Sunday at six. That cat holds a <kanji>grudge</kanji>.
怨.on: Above all, she hates that mower's rattling <sound>en</sound>gine.
怨.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>, hur<sound>rah</sound>,' she purrs each Sunday, admiring her paw prints.

串.meaning: A greedy giant at a picnic can't wait for his lunch. He spears two square sandwiches straight through the <part>middle</part> on one long stick, then posts them into his <part>mouth</part>, one after the other. Lunch on a <kanji>skewer</kanji>.
串.on: He wears a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation in his hat while he eats.
串.kun: His <sound>coo</sound>k feeds the leftover crusts to a <sound>shee</sound>p.

勅.meaning: A messenger who is all <part>muscle</part> sprints through every village with a <part>bundle</part> of scrolls on his back, nailing one to each door: 'From today, all cats must be called Your Majesty.' Nobody argues with an <kanji>imperial order</kanji>.
勅.on: The palace pays him in bars of <sound>choc</sound>olate.
勅.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat reads it aloud to a <sound>ko</sound>ala, who drops his <sound>to</sound>ffee, ties a <sound>kno</sound>t in his scarf and runs off to tell the fish on the <sound>ree</sound>f.

斑.meaning: A <part>dancer</part> twirls between two <part>king</part> twins as they paint the ballroom, one in red and one in yellow. Every spin flicks paint off her skirt onto the walls, the floor and the kings' beards. By the end, the whole palace is <kanji>mottled</kanji>.
斑.on: A bee flies in and mistakes the yellow spots for <sound>hon</sound>ey.
斑.kun: The dancer flops down, dizzy, on a spotty <sound>fu</sound>ton.

玩.meaning: A grumpy <part>king</part> won't sign any laws until his carpenter brings him a <part>sawhorse</part> with a painted head and a mop for a tail. He gallops it round the throne room, neighing, all afternoon. The court calls it the royal steed. It's a <kanji>toy</kanji>.
玩.on: Its legs get clogged with <sound>gun</sound>k from the castle moat.
玩.kun: He polishes it with a <sound>mo</sound>p, feeds it <sound>chee</sound>se, sighs '<sound>Ah</sound>,' and tucks it in on the <sound>so</sound>fa.
